newsitem.title: UK: Britain to keep 5,000 troops in Bosnia next year.
newsitem.headline: Britain to keep 5,000 troops in Bosnia next year.

text.p: Britain said on Wednesday it was ready to keep 5,000 heavily-armed ground troops in Bosnia next year as part of an international peacekeeping force.
The Ministry of Defence said the troops would be part of a "follow on" force expected to replace the current NATO-led peace force, whose mandate expires at the end of next month.
The new British force would be equipped with Challenger tanks, Scimitar armoured reconnaissance vehicles, track mounted artillery and Warrior armoured fighting vehicles, a ministry spokesman said.
These ground forces would be backed up in the air by Harrier, Tornado and Jaguar combat aircraft.

The spokesman said the commitment of forces by Defence Secretary Michael Portillo depended on what NATO planners ultimately decided would be necessary and the readiness of other nations to contribute to the new peacekeeping force.

Britain, which currently has around 8,000 troops in Bosnia as part of the 55,000-strong IFOR force, hosts an international conference on the civilian aspects of peace implementation in Bosnia on Wednesday and Thursday of next week.
